significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that a model’s vector of acquired-trait strengths—its "susceptibility fingerprint"—predictively couples to its base-model ancestry and remains informative across specified derivative transformations, thereby fixing expectations about which reference signal an unlabelled derivative will absorb. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a proposed geometry-linked mechanism, and it would turn the matched-base regularity reported in Cloud et al., "Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data," into a quantitative lineage relation rather than merely showing that transfer exists. A verified-false result would still rule out matched-base subliminal susceptibility as a robust lineage invariant under fine-tuning, quantization, or distillation, although it would not by itself distinguish all possible reasons for failure; true and false therefore name determinate and meaningfully different states of the world. Topic substitution fails: merely proposing to extend subliminal learning would not yield this ancestry-prediction law or constrain provenance explanations, so the score is earned by the claim-specific coupling rather than the topic’s general importance.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "susceptibility fingerprint," a quantitative vector intended to support "forensic attribution of derivative/fine-tuned models"; it is primarily a diagnostic of an already-existing lineage rather than an ex-ante forecast of a future failure, but it provides an action window for supply-chain auditors before trusting or shipping a model. After per-model probing, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—high susceptibility to references sharing base ancestry and low susceptibility otherwise—rather than merely supplying an unconstrained procedure for searching, with asserted scope across model families, fine-tuned derivatives, quantization, instruction tuning, and distillation. Its downstream users could include model auditors and deployers, satisfying non-researcher uptake, though the requirement for short fine-tuning access and possible erosion under heavy transformation limit applicability to pure query-only services. Topic substitution again fails: the generic subliminal-learning topic supplies neither this lineage handle nor its predicted own-family/cross-family ordering, so the reach comes from the specific forensic conclusion.
